evidence_quotes.agenda: 'What are your biggest concerns on this move?' — asked early, right after the move date, before logistics probing began.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer's stated concern was getting her furniture safely loaded for a long out-of-town drive to Dallas; the rep gave a direct, relevant reassurance about wrapping/blanket protection but didn't probe further into which specific pieces worried her most.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: Call is incomplete for grading purposes — flagging a genuine call-type ambiguity: this is a long-distance/out-of-town move, and the rep cleanly and correctly escalates it to a pricing specialist before ever reaching the differentiator pitch or estimate ('I will go ahead and endorse your profile to a specialist who can quote this accurately since this is an out-of-town move'). This is a proper, by-design handoff, not an abandoned call, but it doesn't match the rubric's specific walkthrough_scheduler carve-out (which is defined only for large-move virtual walkthroughs), so Stage 2/3 items are scored as 0 rather than N/A.

top_strength: Extraordinary patience across a 36-minute call with a very talkative, still-undecided customer (unconfirmed move-out date, unconfirmed destination address, a hard-to-describe fireplace TV stand) — never once rushed her and handled a pointed 'are you guys expensive' question gracefully.
coaching_note: Worth confirming with Amanda whether out-of-town escalation calls like this one should get a similar N/A treatment to walkthrough-scheduler calls in a future rubric revision, since a good rep gets penalized here purely for correctly routing a move type they aren't meant to quote themselves.
